featured.name: Gamex
featured.summary: A TypeScript 2D engine with a browser studio where scenes, sprites, UI, and effects are built in one place.
featured.problem: Making a game means jumping between separate tools for assets, scenes, behavior, and UI.
featured.built: A 2D engine and browser-based studio with scene, sprite, and UI editors, WebGL2 effects, a shared command API, and an embedded AI agent — tested by building a real game in it.
featured.flavor: A forge for small worlds. Every tool it holds was made to build the next.
featured.note: Private repository — case study and captures only. Alpha software; usability hasn’t been measured with outside users yet.

projects.name: Reliquary of Ash
projects.summary: A gothic vampire roguelite with sword-and-hex combat, build choices, and a boss waiting at the end.
projects.problem: Gamex needed a real game to show where its workflows broke down.
projects.built: A three-room browser prototype built in Gamex, ending at the Bell Warden. A newer standalone Godot version adds manual sword combat, automatic relics, boss boons, and procedurally streamed survival rounds.
projects.flavor: Ash remembers the shape of what burned. So does the bell.
projects.note: Development captures, not final art. Keyboard recommended for the prototype.

projects.name: After School Spirits
projects.summary: Recruit neighborhood spirits, arrange a three-creature team on a school courtyard grid, and watch real-time battles unfold.
projects.problem: Could the Pixel3D visual presets carry a complete, standalone game?
projects.built: A Godot prototype with team preparation on an 8×8 courtyard, continuous grid combat, rewards, duplicate training, charms, a shop, and saved expeditions — plus switchable GBA, Sakuranbo, and FL3 color filters.
projects.flavor: Small spirits linger where children once played. Some can be talked into a fight.
projects.note: Original low-poly creatures and environment. Interface art made with PixelLab and Aseprite.

projects.name: Pixel3D
projects.summary: A look-development sandbox for low-poly worlds with pixel palettes, lighting, weather, and stacked screen effects.
projects.problem: How far can a real-time 3D scene be pushed toward a hand-made pixel-art look?
projects.built: Three explorable scenes — a forest, a woodland kingdom, and a Japanese school — plus an overlay editor for palettes, ordered effect stacks, vegetation, shadows, weather, undo/redo, and saved looks.
projects.flavor: Three small worlds, and one lantern to see them all by.
projects.note: Rendering work adapts supplied compositor effects alongside original environment and interaction work. These are studies, not released games.

projects.name: Is This a Sandwich?
projects.summary: Build improbable sandwiches to satisfy picky customers, growing your deck through rewards, markets, and workshop upgrades.
projects.problem: Deckbuilders get hard to follow when many effects stack at once.
projects.built: A Godot roguelite with three chefs, twelve customers over three days, ingredient levels, fusion, and enchantments — plus seeded runs, resumable shifts, and a step-by-step scoring breakdown.
projects.flavor: Bread, filling, bread. The customers will argue about everything else.

paragraphs: I’m Newton, a Seattle developer who came to code the long way — through digital media arts, graphic design, and managing a busy tea shop. Today I build full-stack internal platforms at Lyft, and in my own time I build game engines, prototypes, and pixel-art worlds.
I like tools that get out of the way and games that pull you in. Both come down to understanding the person on the other side of the screen.
Away from the keyboard, I lead youth programs in my community and tinker with tabletop game design.

roles.title: Application Support Specialist (Contract)
bullets: Build full-stack internal platforms for the Connected Experience team, used in employee workflows across the company.
Create Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers that bring AI tools into everyday employee work.
Maintain the Slack bot infrastructure behind several internal services.

roles.title: IT Support Intern
bullets: Contributed front-end and full-stack work to more than four internal software projects.
Supported Mac and PC users, networks, device provisioning, and onboarding; wrote troubleshooting guides and procedures.
Ran daily IT Support stand-ups and joined biweekly sprint planning and retros.

items.text: Led six mentors and built curriculum for ages 14–17. Organized two volunteer events that raised $10,000 for nonprofits.
Supervised a 12-person team serving up to 400 guests at peak, and helped open a new location.
Ran scheduling, onboarding, and daily operations for a team of 10–12.
Led a creative team producing an outreach animation for the Bellevue Stream Team.
Pitched and produced a bilingual English/Spanish health campaign in Adobe Creative Suite.
